Gleick ORCID: orcid.org/0000-0001-7232-9284 3 , Jahan Taganova ORCID: orcid.org/0009-0009-9808-943X 4 , Syed Mohammad Ali 5 , 6 , Yueming Yan ORCID: orcid.org/0000-0002-5704-0308 7 & … Ambika Vishwanath ORCID: orcid.org/0009-0003-1032-4682 8 , 9 Show authors Nature Water ( 2026 ) Cite this article Save article View saved research 29 Accesses 3 Altmetric Metrics details Abstract The ongoing conflict between India and Pakistan, heightened by the April 2025 terrorist attack in Pahalgam, Kashmir, has led to an unprecedented abeyance of India’s participation in the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT). Although this treaty has often been described as an example of hydrological cooperation despite regional conflict, it has systemic problems from the perspective of long-term environmental, political and social sustainability. We identify several factors that justify renegotiating and revising the IWT, leveraging multilateral and domestic policy frameworks to formulate a more effective and comprehensive agreement. This includes metrics set forth on transboundary water cooperation under the Sustainable Development Goals (Indicator 6.5.2) as well as a range of international legal guidelines for drafting ecologically viable treaties. We explore the role that nascent regional organizations could play in reducing tensions over the Indus Basin and facilitating new discussions. Ultimately, a reset in the IWT could catalyse broader confidence-building and a lasting peace in a region where two nuclear rivals share a 3,200-km-long contiguous border.
